# Account, company profile, usage and team

`GET /v1/whoami` names the workspace and whether the credential can write. The company profile is the classifier's context and the biggest lever on relevance. Usage shows the balance, the burn, days left and the cost per keyword, platform, group or day. Team changes need a signed-in owner or admin, so an API key answers `403` there. Don't create API keys unless asked.

Base URL `https://api.rumoro.dev`, `Authorization: Bearer $RUMORO_API_KEY` on every request, JSON in and out. Each endpoint names its `rumoro` CLI command for when the CLI is installed (rules/cli.md).

## Endpoints

### `GET /v1/health`: getHealth

Checks that the API is up. Needs no key and is not rate limited. Returns `ok: true` with the state of the database and each background worker.

CLI: `rumoro system:health`

Answers `200` with `ok`: The API is running.

### `GET /v1/company`: Get the company profile

Returns what the classifier knows about your company. That is the name, description, use cases and your accounts, plus the context text built from them.

CLI: `rumoro company:get`

Answers `200` with `name`, `description`, `useCases`, `accounts`, `website`, `competitors`, `guidelines`, `context`: Your company profile.

### `PATCH /v1/company`: Update the company profile

Changing profile fields rebuilds the classifier's context. Setting `context` yourself replaces it until the next profile change. New mentions are scored with the change right away.

CLI: `rumoro company:update`

Body (JSON):

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string |  |  |
| `description` | string |  |  |
| `useCases` | string[] |  | Sets the full new list. |
| `accounts` | object |  |  |
| `accounts.x` | string or null |  |  |
| `accounts.linkedin` | string or null |  |  |
| `website` | string or null |  | The company's website. Null removes it. |
| `competitors` | string[] |  | Sets the full new list. An empty list clears it. |
| `guidelines` | string or null |  | Rules for the classifier in your own words. Null removes them. |
| `context` | string |  | Replaces the built context until the next profile change. |

Answers `200` with `name`, `description`, `useCases`, `accounts`, `website`, `competitors`, `guidelines`, `context`: The profile after the change.

### `GET /v1/api-keys`: List API keys

Lists the workspace's active keys, latest first, with name, prefix, scope, expiry and last use. Revoked keys and secrets are never listed.

CLI: `rumoro api-keys:list`

Answers `200` with `data`: All keys, latest first, without the secret.

### `POST /v1/api-keys`: Create an API key

Issues a new API key in this workspace. The key is shown only in this response, and only its hash is stored. `expiresAt` makes it stop working at a set time, useful for a contractor or a one-off script. An expired key stays in the list until you revoke it.

CLI: `rumoro api-keys:create`

Body (JSON):

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string |  | A name for the key. Defaults to "default". |
| `scope` | `read`, `write` |  | write can do everything. read is limited to GET. |
| `expiresAt` | string |  | Expiry time in ISO 8601 or epoch ms, later than now. Set it for keys you hand to a script or contractor. Omit it or send null and the key never expires. |

Answers `201` with `id`, `name`, `prefix`, `scope`, `createdAt`, `lastUsedAt`, `expiresAt`, `key`: The created key, visible only now.

### `DELETE /v1/api-keys/{id}`: Revoke an API key

Revokes the key. The API refuses it right away, and cached checks catch up within a few minutes.

CLI: `rumoro api-keys:revoke`

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The API key's id (key_...). |

Answers `204`: The key no longer works.

### `GET /v1/whoami`: Check the credential

Call this first. It shows the workspace the credential works in, its type (API key, MCP sign-in token or dashboard session), whether it can write, and for keys the id and expiry. A read key gets 403 read_only_key on any write, and scripts often aim at the wrong workspace.

CLI: `rumoro auth:whoami`

Answers `200` with `workspace`, `auth`, `user`: Details of the credential.

### `GET /v1/members`: List members

Returns all workspace members, owners first. Use `userId` for a mention's assigneeId and a person's ownerId.

CLI: `rumoro members:list`

Answers `200` with `data`: The workspace's members.

### `GET /v1/members/invitations`: List pending invitations

Returns invitations that have not been accepted, declined or expired yet. Once accepted, the person shows up in GET /v1/members.

CLI: `rumoro members:invitations`

Answers `200` with `data`: The pending invitations.

### `POST /v1/members/invitations`: Invite a member

Invites an address by email as admin or member. Invitations expire after 48 hours. Repeating it for a pending address returns that invitation with 200 and sends nothing. Existing members get 409 already_member. Needs a signed-in owner or admin (dashboard session or MCP sign-in token). API keys get 403.

CLI: `rumoro members:invite`

Body (JSON):

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | string | yes | Address that receives the join link. |
| `role` | `admin`, `member` |  | The role they get when they join. Ownership can only be given in the dashboard. |

Answers `200` with `id`, `email`, `role`, `invitedBy`, `expiresAt`, `createdAt`: The pending invitation for this address; `201` with `id`, `email`, `role`, `invitedBy`, `expiresAt`, `createdAt`: The invitation that was emailed.

### `DELETE /v1/members/invitations/{id}`: Revoke an invitation

Cancels the invitation, and its email link stops working right away. Needs a signed-in owner or admin. An API key gets 403.

CLI: `rumoro members:revoke-invitation`

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The invitation's id (inv_...). |

Answers `204`: The key no longer works.

### `DELETE /v1/members/{id}`: Remove a member

Needs a signed-in owner or admin. Admins can't remove owners, and the last owner can't be removed at all (409 last_owner). Access ends within a minute, at the next dashboard request or when the OAuth token's short cache expires. The member's mentions, notes and outreach records remain.

CLI: `rumoro members:remove`

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The membership's id (mem_...). |

Answers `204`: Done.

### `GET /v1/usage`: Get usage and balance

Shows whether tracking is stopped or the balance is low. Also returns the prepaid balance (ledger total, pending mention charges, and the effective balance that decides pausing), daily spend and days left, running and paused keywords, and matches today and over 30 days. Pricing is $0.008 per matched mention, relevant or not, and $5 a month per active keyword, charged daily.

CLI: `rumoro usage:get`

Answers `200` with `balance`, `burn`, `keywords`, `mentions`, `stopped`, `lowBalance`, `lastTopUpAt`: A summary of usage.

### `GET /v1/usage/breakdown`: Get the usage breakdown

Returns what the workspace used and was charged over a period, in US cents at list price. Each call groups rows by one `by` value, day, platform or keyword, and always includes the totals. `range` reads the past UTC days up to today (30d by default). `month` reads one calendar month (YYYY-MM), which is what you match against a bill or a per-client margin. Keyword-days come from the daily run and mention charges from billed matches. So a deleted keyword keeps its charges in the keyword rows (`keyword.removed`), while its mention counts show 0. Each keyword carries the same numbers for the current month as `stats.cost`. `totals.ledgerDebitCents` is what the balance has been debited so far for the period's days. Mentions settle the morning after, so a period ending today is below `totals.totalCents` by the unsettled ones, and a finished month differs only by cumulative rounding. Rows come in pages (`limit`, `offset`, `total`). A workspace can call this 30 times a minute across all its keys and tokens.

CLI: `rumoro usage:breakdown`

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `by` | query | `day`, `platform`, `keyword`, `group` |  | How to group the rows. day gives one row per UTC day, then platform, keyword (the default, used to work out margins), or group (the cost of a client or campaign). |
| `range` | query | `7d`, `30d`, `90d` |  | How many UTC days back from today to read. One of 7d, 30d or 90d, 30d by default. Ignored when you send `month`. |
| `month` | query | string |  | A calendar month (YYYY-MM, UTC) to read instead of a range. It covers the month's first to last day, or up to today for the current month. A future month returns 400. |
| `limit` | query | integer |  | How many rows to return, from 1 to 500, 100 by default. Only by=keyword can need more than one page, since a period has at most 90 days and there are only a dozen platforms. |
| `offset` | query | integer or null |  | How many rows to skip. |

Answers `200` with `window`, `by`, `currency`, `totals`, `data`, `total`: The period's totals and a page of rows.

### `POST /v1/billing/top-ups`: Start a top-up

Returns a hosted checkout link with `amountCents` filled in. The buyer can change it there, from $20 to $5,000. The balance is credited within a minute of payment, and tracking paused for balance resumes right away. This call charges nothing by itself. `successUrl` must be on an origin this deployment trusts. Leave it out to return to the dashboard's billing page.

CLI: `rumoro billing:top-up`

Body (JSON):

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `amountCents` | integer | yes | The amount to add in US cents, from 2000 to 500000. Checkout starts with it and the buyer can change it. |
| `successUrl` | string |  | Page to return to after payment. It must be on an origin this deployment trusts, like the dashboard, and defaults to the dashboard's billing page. |

Answers `200` with `url`: A checkout link with the amount filled in.

### `GET /v1/billing/wallet`: Get the balance

Returns every detail of the prepaid balance. That covers the ledger total, pending mention charges, the effective balance used for pausing, the daily spend and days left, running and paused keywords, the cost of a day and of resuming, the welcome credit, the latest top-up, the top-up limits and the auto-recharge settings. `GET /v1/usage` gives a shorter version.

CLI: `rumoro billing:wallet`

Answers `200` with `balanceCents`, `pendingCents`, `effectiveBalanceCents`, `burnPerDayCents`, `daysLeft`, `stopped`, `lowBalance`, `activeKeywords`, `autoMutedKeywords`, `nextDayCents`, `resumeCostCents`, `signupCredit`, `lastTopUpAt`, `billingConfigured`, `minTopUpCents`, `maxTopUpCents`, `defaultTopUpCents`, `currency`, `autoRecharge`: Wallet balance, daily spend and pause state.

### `GET /v1/billing/ledger`: List ledger entries

Shows the balance's history, latest first. Entries cover the welcome credit, top-ups, refunds, adjustments, and the daily keyword-day and mention debits. Debits carry their UTC settlement day and cumulative units. Cursor pages.

CLI: `rumoro billing:ledger`

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cursor` | query | string |  | The `nextCursor` of the previous page. Do not parse it. |
| `limit` | query | integer |  | How many to return, from 1 to 100, 25 by default. |

Answers `200` with `data`, `nextCursor`: Ledger entries, latest first.

### `GET /v1/billing/invoices`: List receipts

Returns the top-up orders, latest first, as Polar, the merchant of record, stores them. You get this workspace's orders among the billing customer's latest 100. No orders exist before the first top-up.

CLI: `rumoro billing:invoices`

Answers `200` with `data`: Receipts for paid orders. Empty before the first payment.

### `GET /v1/billing/invoices/{id}/url`: Get a receipt link

For a paid order from GET /v1/billing/invoices, returns a receipt PDF URL that expires soon.

CLI: `rumoro billing:invoice-url`

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | Which paid order. Ids come from GET /v1/billing/invoices. |

Answers `200` with `url`: Receipt PDF URL, valid briefly.
